answer: That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, because each alias restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's forge standing. Because the saffron record is per identity, the cipher audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. Promotion out of probation needs 14 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. That is 15 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
